title: MetaAudit: Reproducibility Capsule for Automated Meta-Analytic Quality Audits
author: Mahmood Ahmad
body: Can a reproducibility capsule turn an evidence-synthesis repository into a reviewer-auditable submission without restaging the workflow? We audited the shipped project using 27 source files, 18 test files, 10 manuscript or guide files, and 7 dashboard or figure assets committed locally. The capsule packages a micro-paper, a machine-readable config, an interactive reader, and a protocol so the repository can be inspected across reviewers. Across the inventory, the repository yields a documentation proportion of 0.16, with file-count range 7-27 across core surfaces, while exposing 8 entry points and 5 declared dependencies. Git metadata, file counts, and copied assets provide a stable local audit trail even when engine outputs remain outside the submission bundle. This packaging step converts a diffuse codebase into a citable, inspectable micro-publication suitable for rapid editorial triage and downstream peer review. The capsule does not verify scientific correctness itself; it standardizes what reviewers receive first, and deeper validation still depends on tests and manuscripts.

notes.data: Repository inventory with 27 source files, 18 test files, 10 documents, and 7 assets.

checks.name: single paragraph
checks.detail: Body must not contain blank-line paragraph breaks.

checks.name: no headings
checks.detail: No markdown headings allowed in body.

checks.name: no links
checks.detail: No links or DOI links allowed in body.

checks.name: result sentence has interval
checks.detail: Sentence 4 should include a quantitative result such as a percentage, count, or interval.

checks.name: result sentence has estimand
checks.detail: Sentence 4 should name an effect measure or test metric.

checks.name: boundary sentence present
checks.detail: Sentence 7 should express a limitation, harm, or scope boundary.
